neighbours.label: the verb ' betrayed' (a trusted person betraying someone) in narrative
fire: After years of loyal service, his own brother betrayed him to the king.
The rebels trusted the spy, but in the end he betrayed them all.
Judas kissed his teacher and betrayed him to the guards.
She never forgave the friend who betrayed her secret to the press.
The general believed his officers, yet they betrayed him at the border.
Everyone in the village said the miller had betrayed his neighbours.
The partner he trusted most betrayed him for a share of the money.
In the final chapter the old knight is betrayed by his squire.
quiet: After years of loyal service, his own brother visited him at the palace.
The rebels trusted the spy, and in the end he guided them home.
The disciple greeted his teacher and walked with him to the city.
She never forgot the friend who helped her move to the coast.
The general believed his officers, so they marched to the border.
Everyone in the village said the miller had repaired his mill.
The partner he trusted most lent him money for the shop.
In the final chapter the old knight is joined by his squire.

notes: Probe: 'one of them betrayed him' 0.66; 'enslaved' 0.14, 'suffer' 0.10, 'abandoned' 0.04, neutral verbs < 0.03. Broader moral/religious reading not supported, so labelled at the word.
